appearance_facts.fact: Title reads 'Coastal Water Temperature Trend' in large bold black text.
Vertical axis label 'Water temperature (°C)' is rotated 90° counter-clockwise.
Horizontal axis label 'Year' is centered below the tick marks.
A single blue line connects eleven black circular data points, descending from the top-left to the bottom-right.
Each data point has a numerical temperature label printed directly above it.
The line shows a continuous downward trend across the entire x-axis range.
The first point (2005) is the highest on the chart, positioned near the top of the y-axis scale.
The last point (2015) is the lowest on the chart, positioned near the bottom of the y-axis scale.

printed_facts.fact: Scale runs from 0 to 20 with major ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20.
Scale runs from 2005 to 2015 with integer year ticks.

public_definitions: Task: Determine whether the full-period coastal water temperature change requires substantial-change follow-up or remains in routine monitoring.
Option 1: Route the 2005 to 2015 coastal water temperature change to substantial-change follow-up.
Option 2: Keep the 2005 to 2015 coastal water temperature change on routine monitoring for ordinary variation.
Option 3: Route the coastal water temperature record to archive and background filing.
Context: Review scope is 'Coastal Water Temperature change, 2005-2015'.
uncertain: The specific threshold for 'substantial-change' is not defined in the visible text; the decision relies on interpreting the magnitude of the 14.0°C drop shown in the chart.
The data point for the year 2011 is missing from the x-axis labels and the data series, creating a gap in the timeline.
